rationale:
`UsageLog` (src/authoring/usage.rs, lines 77–84) is an in-memory handle for one run's usage record. It holds the `UsageRecord`, the record's file `path`, and private bookkeeping (`started`, `seen`, `active_request`). The struct is not serialized, so it does not itself define the record's fields or format. It also decides nothing about the record's location or contents.

The parts of `requirements.authoring.usage_storage` that need implementing are done elsewhere:
- **Record fields:** `UsageRecord` (lines 14–43) is marked `{impl}` for `usage_storage` and holds the version, run, project root, subject, start and end times, outcome, determination, `evidence_output` and `evidence_written` fields.
- **Path and file creation:** `UsageLog::start` builds `<state>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` and creates the file. It is also marked `{impl}`.
- **Finishing and saving:** `finish` and `save` are marked `{impl}`.

The struct pairs the record with its storage path, so a change to the requirement's storage or record model could force a change to it. That makes `{cite}` the right role. It has no `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the same requirement, so the citation is not redundant.

text: Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
